subject: MSA & Order Form: triage on third-party claim defend/control split
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-21 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: MSA / Order Form — defense/control split question

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the redlines. Two specific items our legal team is pushing back on and asked me to raise directly:

1) Third‑party IP claims (patent/copyright) — they want Redwood to "defend and control" for any claims arising from the use of the service by Acme, including model output that allegedly infringes third‑party IP.
2) Reimbursement vs defend — Acme is proposing a defend‑and‑indemnify approach for model‑output claims but wants Redwood limited to reimbursement for other types of claims (e.g., data ingestion or customer configuration).

Our procurement counsel (Amy Li, cc'd) suggested we confirm Redwood's practical posture here before we escalate to our GC. Can you confirm: does Redwood accept defend‑and‑control for third‑party claims tied to model output? If not, what on‑ramps/guardrails (notice, cooperation, cap, ability to select counsel) would you propose as a compromise?

We have an internal timeline to get the executed order by end of this month, so any quick clarification helps.

Thanks —
Sam (on behalf of Acme procurement)
Procurement Team
Acme Corp

Attachments: none
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Amy Li <amy.li@novuslegal.com>
Date: 2028-10-21 10:05 AM -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — defense/control split question

Sam —

Appreciate the clarity. Short answer: we are open to defend‑and‑control for narrowly scoped third‑party IP claims tied directly to model output (i.e., claims that assert the output itself infringes), but there are several operational and legal guardrails we need to keep in place. High level of what we need:

- Narrow trigger: claim must relate to the model output used by the customer, not the customer's data, configuration, or how they integrated the model.
- Notice and cooperation: prompt written notice, right to assume defense, cooperation and control over counsel selection (Redwood-led, subject to conflict rules).
- Mitigation / injunctive risk: we need the ability to implement mitigations (model prompt guardrails, rate limits, temporary disabling of endpoints) if injunctive relief is sought.
- Cap and exclusions: cap tied to order form value or insurance threshold; carve out for bad‑faith or willful misconduct by the customer.

Kimberly — I've attached a proposed mark for the Order Form with language that reflects this compromise (OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Amy — curious if that aligns with Acme's expectations.

If this sounds like a path we can take, I'd like to schedule a 30‑minute call today to walk the exact wording and the notice SLA that Acme needs.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (PDF)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Amy Li <amy.li@novuslegal.com>
Date: 2028-10-21 13:45 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — defense/control split question

Folks —

Quick legal POV and proposed redline notes inline below. High‑level positions:

1) We can accept defend‑and‑control for third‑party claims about model output, limited as Irene described.
2) We should avoid an uncapped defend‑and‑indemnify for anything that isn't tied to output (customer data ingestion, custom models trained on customer content, or customer misuse). Instead propose: reimbursement model or carveouts.

Specifics I added to OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf:
- Definition: "Infringement Claim" means a claim alleging the customer's receipt or use of the Model Output infringes a third party's intellectual property.
- Remedy: Redwood shall defend and pay those costs up to the lesser of (i) the amount available under Redwood's insurance and (ii) the Order Form cap.
- Control: Redwood may assume exclusive control of the defense; customer may participate at its own cost; Redwood to notify customer within 15 days of receipt of claim.
- Injunctive relief: Redwood may take technical mitigations; remedies do not include obligations to indemnify for consequences of injunction including lost revenue.
- Evidence cooperation: Customer to provide logs, prompts, and materials necessary to investigate; Redwood will maintain a triage evidence binder (see evidence‑sla‑matrix.xlsx).

Attachments: evidence-sla-matrix.xlsx (XLSX)

I recommend we propose this compromise to Acme and, if accepted in principle, lock the cap discussion into the order form (i.e., numeric cap per year rather than open ended).

— Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>, Amy Li <amy.li@novuslegal.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-21 16:40 PM -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — defense/control split question

Sam/Amy —

Thanks for raising. To be explicit about next steps from Redwood's side:

1) We are willing to accept defend‑and‑control for narrowly scoped "Infringement Claims" that are based on Model Output, subject to the cap/insurance linkage Kimberly proposed and cooperation requirements.
2) For other claim types (data ingestion, config, customer‑trained artifacts) we propose reimbursement or explicit carveouts.
3) On a pragmatic level, we propose a two‑week onboarding checklist if Acme accepts this approach:
   - Exchange of contact points + SOC2 evidence (if not already provided)
   - Agreed evidence collection path (logs, prompt archive) — we will maintain the triage binder and share redacted extracts on request
   - Interim mitigation plan: Redwood will attempt non‑disruptive mitigations for suspected output issues; emergency mitigations may be applied with notice.

If Acme is ok in principle, let's set a 30‑minute call tomorrow with Amy + our legal team to nail the exact language and numeric cap. If they need a stronger remedy (uncapped defend) we should escalate to our GC for signoff.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Legal Operations (contracts escalation)
marissa.cole@redwood.com
